title: Grand Duchy of Baden
capsule: The Grand Duchy of Baden was proclaimed on 25 July 1806 when the Margraviate of Baden was elevated by Napoleon in exchange for Baden's adhesion to the Confederation of the Rhine; its first grand duke was Charles Frederick, who had ruled Baden since 1738. Under Grand Duke Leopold (r. 1830–1852) Baden became a center of German liberal constitutionalism, and the revolution of 1848–49 produced the most radical popular government in German states before its suppression by Prussian troops. Baden sided with Prussia in the 1866 Austro-Prussian War and joined the North German Confederation, becoming one of the founding states of the German Empire proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871, whereupon the grand duchy continued as a constituent kingdom within unified Germany until 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries of the Grand Duchy are well documented through successive German federal acts and cadastral surveys; some border adjustments with Württemberg and Bavaria in the early 19th century are precisely recorded.
